extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions, and exercises about δ‑functors, derived functors, spectral sequences, and cohomology of sheaves (including Čech vs derived functor cohomology and Leray). Intended as textbook guidance and proof-sketches for computations and conceptual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: δ-functor: short-exact→long-exact (exactness property)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (cohomological) δ-functor is a collection of additive functors T^i : A → B (T^i = 0 for i < 0) together with morphisms δ^i : T^i(A'') → T^{i+1}(A') for each short exact sequence 0 → A' → A → A'' → 0, satisfying that for each such short exact sequence the sequence ... → T^{i-1}(A'') --δ^{i-1}→ T^i(A') → T^i(A) → T^i(A'') --δ^i→ T^{i+1}(A') → ... is exact. In particular T^0 is left-exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental exactness axiom for δ-functors; the unlabeled maps come from functoriality/covariance of the T^i. Use this to recover the long exact cohomology sequences one expects from derived functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: δ-functor: functoriality of δ-maps
rubrics_metrics.description: For every morphism of short exact sequences (commuting squares) in A, the δ^i's must give a commutative diagram relating the corresponding long exact sequences (i.e., the connecting homomorphisms are natural with respect to maps of short exact sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the long exact sequences produced by the δ-functor are natural in morphisms; it is needed to make δ-functors compatible with diagrams and to define morphisms of δ-functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal δ-functor (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A δ-functor (T^i, δ^i) is universal if for any other δ-functor (T'^i, δ'^i) and any natural transformation α: T^0 → T'^0 there is a unique morphism of δ-functors (T^i, δ^i) → (T'^i, δ'^i) extending α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness follows from the universal property; when a universal δ-functor extending a given left-exact functor F exists it is unique up to unique isomorphism. This is the abstract characterization under which derived functors are canonical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for universality (Theorem 23.2.8 / effaceability)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (T^i, δ^i) is a covariant δ-functor and for every object A in A there exists a monomorphism A → J with T^i(J) = 0 for all i > 0, then (T^i, δ^i) is universal. Equivalently, it suffices that each T^i is effaceable (for every A there is a monomorphism A→J with T^i(J)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the key existence/uniqueness criterion: vanishing of higher T^i on enough objects (or effaceability) implies universality. See references (Weibel, Lang, Grothendieck) for alternate proofs/hints; the exercise is noted to be hard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derived functors form a universal δ-functor when enough injectives exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has enough injectives and F : A → B is a left-exact covariant functor, then the right derived functors R^iF (with their connecting morphisms δ^i) form a universal δ-functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: embed each object into an injective; higher derived functors of an injective vanish because computing via the injective resolution of the injective itself gives zero. This gives the universality via Theorem 23.2.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry of Tor
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor_A^i(M,N) ≅ Tor_A^i(N,M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by taking free resolutions of M and N, building the 'product' double complex, and comparing the two spectral sequences arising from the two filtrations/orientations.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-acyclic objects and acyclic resolutions for computing derived functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right-exact additive functor F : A → B and A has enough projectives, an object A is F-acyclic if L_iF(A) = 0 for i > 0. Derived functors of F can be computed using resolutions by F-acyclic objects (not just projectives): take a resolution ... → A_2 → A_1 → A_0 → B → 0 by F-acyclic objects, apply F and take homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a useful computational trick: flat (or other acyclic) resolutions can be used to compute Tor/derived functors. See Hint 23.3.3 and the construction of a projective resolution of a complex via a double complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck composition-of-functors spectral sequence (statement and hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : A → B and G : B → C are left-exact additive covariant functors, A and B have enough injectives, and F sends injective objects of A to G-acyclic objects of B, then for each X in A there is a spectral sequence with E_2^{p,q} = R^qG(R^pF(X)) converging to R^{p+q}(G∘F)(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key hypotheses: left-exactness, enough injectives in the intermediate categories, and acyclicity condition (F(injectives) are G-acyclic). Remarks: the E_2 page is independent of choices; this theorem yields the Leray spectral sequence as a special case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartan–Eilenberg resolution (existence and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complex C• in an abelian category, one can build a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution: a first-quadrant double complex I_{p,q} of injectives whose rows and columns are exact and such that the complexes Z_p(I•,q), B_p(I•,q), H_p(I•,q) are injective resolutions of Z_p(C•), B_p(C•), H_p(C•) respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses injective resolutions chosen for the homology and boundary pieces and a horseshoe-type construction; see exercises 23.3.E–G. Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions are used to construct the double complex needed in the Grothendieck spectral sequence proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod_OX has enough injectives (Theorem 23.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space (X, O_X), the category Mod_{O_X} of O_X-modules has enough injectives (so derived functors R^iΓ and higher pushforwards exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct injective O_X-modules by taking for each point p an injective O_{X,p}-module Q_p and forming the skyscraper sheaf i_{p,*} Q_p; arbitrary products of injectives are injective; taking the product over points yields an injective sheaf Q' and the natural map F → ∏_p Q_p is injective (by checking stalks). See Exercises 23.4.A–C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: sheaf cohomology via derived functors
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space (X, O_X) and an O_X-module F, define H^i(X, F) := R^i Γ(X, F). For a morphism π : (X, O_X) → (Y, O_Y) define higher pushforwards R^iπ_* : Mod_{O_X} → Mod_{O_Y}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general derived-functor definition of sheaf cohomology and higher direct images; earlier Čech definitions agree in many cases (see §23.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leray spectral sequence (statement and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π : (X, O_X) → (Y, O_Y) of ringed spaces and any O_X-module F, there is a spectral sequence with E_2^{p,q} = H^q(Y, R^pπ_* F) abutting to H^{p+q}(X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the Grothendieck spectral sequence applied to Γ(Y, -) ∘ π_* once one knows π_* sends injectives to Γ(Y,-)-acyclics (i.e., the pushforward of an injective O_X-module is Γ-acyclic). The proof uses that injectives are flasque and flasque sheaves are Γ-acyclic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flasque (flabby) sheaf (definition and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf F on a topological space is flasque if all restriction maps res_{V→U} : F(V) → F(U) are surjective for all U ⊂ V open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences and exercises: (a) If 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 with F' flasque then the sequence on sections over any open U is exact. (b) Pushforwards of flasque sheaves are flasque. (c) Injective sheaves are flasque. (d) Flasque sheaves are Γ-acyclic (H^i(X,F)=0 for i>0). These facts are used to show pushforwards of injectives are acyclic for global sections and to deduce Leray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of flasque sheaf is flasque
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a continuous map (or morphism of ringed spaces) and F is a flasque sheaf on X, then π_* F is a flasque sheaf on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 23.4.E gives the check: restriction maps on π_*F come from restriction on F and remain surjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injective sheaves are flasque
rubrics_metrics.description: Any injective O_X-module Q is flasque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 23.4.F: use the exactness properties of Hom((i_U)!, Q) and the extension-by-zero functor i! to show restriction maps are surjective; see Exercise 2.7.G for the needed adjointness facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flasque implies Γ-acyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is flasque then H^i(X, F) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by embedding F into an injective I (which is flasque), take cokernel G, and use the long exact sequence in cohomology to inductively show higher cohomology vanishes (Exercise 23.4.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod_OX need not have enough projectives (caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: In contrast to injectives, the category Mod_{O_X} need not have enough projectives. Example: take X = P^1_k with the Zariski topology and O_X = constant sheaf Z; there are no enough projectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason by contradiction: assume a surjection from a projective sheaf P → Z; analyze stalk maps at a closed point and show they must be zero by lifting properties, contradicting surjectivity. This shows one cannot always compute left-derived functors by projective resolutions in sheaf categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Čech cohomology equals derived-functor cohomology under quasicompact separated + quasicoherent hypotheses (Theorem 23.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated scheme and F is a quasicoherent sheaf, then Čech cohomology of F (with respect to finite affine covers) agrees with derived-functor cohomology H^i(X, F) = R^iΓ(X,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a double complex mixing an injective resolution and the Čech complex, analyzed via two spectral sequence filtrations. Two key ingredients are (A) injectives have no Čech cohomology for finite covers and (B) on affine schemes, quasicoherent sheaves have vanishing higher derived functor cohomology. Functoriality and compatibility with long exact sequences are treated in exercises 23.5.G–H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient (A): injective (hence flasque) sheaves have no Čech cohomology for finite covers
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is an injective O_X-module and X = ∪_i U_i is a finite open cover, then the Čech cohomology H^i( {U_i}, Q) = 0 for i > 0. More generally, flasque sheaves have trivial higher Čech cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by induction on the number n of opens in the cover using the exactness of short exact sequences of Čech complexes and the sheaf property; see Exercise 23.5.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient (B): quasicoherent sheaves on affine schemes are Γ-acyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is affine and F is quasicoherent on X, then R^iΓ(X,F) = 0 for i>0 (i.e., higher derived functor cohomology vanishes on affines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by induction using an injective resolution and choosing a tailored finite affine cover so that a cohomology class is locally a boundary; spectral-sequence bookkeeping then shows the global class vanishes. This is the essential algebraic input (uses quasicoherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right adjoints to exact functors preserve injectives
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F, G) is an adjoint pair of additive functors between abelian categories and F is exact, then the right adjoint G sends injective objects to injective objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce that restriction of an injective sheaf to an open subset is injective (Exercise 23.5.A and 23.5.B). This is a standard adjointness fact: exactness of left adjoint implies right adjoint preserves injectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and compatibility of the Čech↔derived isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism of Theorem 23.5.1 (Čech cohomology ≅ derived cohomology) can be made functorial in F and respects the long exact sequences in cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 23.5.G and 23.5.H ask to check functoriality and compatibility; the hint is that spectral sequences are functorial in their E_0 page, giving naturality of the resulting identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover-wise Leray criterion for Čech computation (Remark 23.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} is a cover of X such that for every finite intersection of the U_i the derived-functor cohomology of F vanishes in positive degrees, then the cohomology of F can be computed by the Čech complex of that fixed cover (no need to pass to the directed limit over all covers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a useful practical variant of the Leray idea: having local vanishing on intersections suffices to compute global cohomology by the Čech complex for that cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks about working in QCoh_X versus Mod_{O_X}
rubrics_metrics.description: QCoh_X (quasicoherent sheaves) has enough injectives if X is Noetherian (and in fact for any scheme but the general proof is harder). Working in QCoh_X requires additional care (e.g., lack of extension-by-zero inside QCoh makes some arguments harder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one wants to compute H^i or R^iπ_* inside QCoh rather than Mod_{O_X}, extra work is needed to show injectives in QCoh restrict and behave as in Mod_{O_X}; references are given. Theorem 23.5.1 helps by showing R^iπ_* of QCoh objects remain quasicoherent under suitable hypotheses.
